name: cTBS pattern (Huang 2005 timing) at C3, motor cortex
summary: Copies continuous theta-burst timing (Huang et al. 2005): pulse triplets at 50 Hz repeated at 5 Hz without a pause for 40 s, 200 bursts and 600 pulses, on one coil at C3 over the left motor cortex. TMS works at 0.5 to 2 tesla; this helmet is at least 60,000 times weaker at 20 mm, so this is a timing pattern only.
notes: Huang 2005: 'In the continuous theta burst stimulation paradigm (cTBS), a 40 s train of uninterrupted TBS is given (600 pulses)' (p.2 [202]). The bursts are 3 pulses at 50 Hz repeated at 5 Hz, at 80% of active motor threshold, with biphasic pulses of about 300 us (Suppa 2008 p.2). The coil sat on the TMS hot spot of the first dorsal interosseous muscle, not on a 10-20 site (Huang 2005 p.5 [205]; Suppa 2008 p.2 [4490]). At TMS strength Huang 2005 reported an inhibitory after-effect on the motor cortex. This program plays the same timing on one coil at C3 with no fade, so all 200 bursts run at full strength. C3 is a scalp approximation of the hand area: Kirimoto 2016 (p.5) puts a hand hot spot 2 to 3 cm in front of C3. Use C4 for the right side. Each TMS pulse becomes +A for 0.5 ms then -A for 0.5 ms, since shorter shapes cannot be resolved at 2 kHz. No cited source gives the TMS coil's field for these experiments; Dufor 2019 states the general range as '0.5 to 2 Tesla' (p.1), with no place of measurement. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. There the helmet is 60,000 to 240,000 times weaker, even at its maximum. The evidence for cTBS belongs to TMS strength. In the one cited test at low intensity, cTBS at 10 mT did nothing (Dufor 2019 p.2, rodent work). No data exist at uT, so do not expect or claim inhibition. It is not a treatment. Not for people with epilepsy; stop if you feel unwell.
schedule: One block per sitting; no schedule has been tested at uT.
source: Huang et al. 2005, Neuron https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15664172/ ; Suppa et al. 2008, J Physiol (iTBS and cTBS definitions) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2614023/ ; Dufor et al. 2019, Sci Adv (rodent low-intensity rTMS) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6821463/
